findings.reason: the section should be collapsed to its unlanded residue (nova's declaration and one real wave close) and its owner named.
findings.text: §6 delivers "project configuration declares its suite command and a whole-run budget" and a tier-none/light hold on a bad run, but that machinery already exists and is live: the review.suite flight key (reckon/schema/flight.yaml:897), the runner and hold predicate (reckon/crew/standing_suite.py) and the gate wiring (reckon/crew/promotion.py:4992 _require_standing_suite) — the section cites none of them, so an implementer reading it verbatim rebuilds a subsystem the plan has already landed

findings.reason: an unnamed owner invites a second suite-config path beside the landed one, which is the duplicate this item exists to catch.
findings.text: §6 is written as if the standing suite is new work, but the owner already ships it: signature command + whole-run budget declared in `review.suite`, one JSON record per run under the project state dir, hold_reason for tiers none/light, and a waiver path; reckon itself already declares the suite in docs/state/reckon/flight.yaml — the section must name reckon/crew/standing_suite.py as the mechanism to extend, not re-specify it

findings.reason: the section must account for the interface surface it adds, whether by naming a retirement or by collapsing to the landed key it reuses.
findings.text: §6 adds a project suite-configuration surface (the review.suite slot and the ReviewSuite class, both already landed) and states no retirement, merge or "nothing can be" for the added public definition surface

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the tier rule is hidden behind review_tier()/changes_runtime_source() in a 106-line reckon/review_tiers.py and the round composition behind compose_repair_for_run() in reckon/crew/repair.py (538 lines), each a small interface over substantial behaviour.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 re-states a standing-suite declaration and a tier-none/light promotion hold that reckon/crew/standing_suite.py already owns and that promotion._require_standing_suite already wires into the gate, and the section names no owner to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §6 adds a project suite-configuration surface (review.suite / the ReviewSuite class) without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be, where §2 does name its retirement (the role check in _require_review_waiver).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 and §3 carry real reuse maps that name the mechanisms they extend (reckon/path_classes.py for the tier classifier, recover/repair for the reflex), but §6 proposes a project suite declaration and hold that already exist in the tree it ships from, and the section cites no owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — neither new module forwards to an existing mechanism without adding behaviour: the resolver adds the tier rule (spec level, size ceiling, elevated risk) over path_classes' path classification, and repair.py mints stable finding ids and round identity rather than wrapping the dispatch path.
